subject: Physics
description: Lenses, mirrors, refraction, human eye, optical instruments

questions.stem: A ray of light travelling in air enters a denser medium such as glass. The ray bends:
questions.explanation: When light enters a denser medium, its speed decreases and it bends towards the normal (Snell's law: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, so if n₂ > n₁, then θ₂ < θ₁). Going the other way — denser to rarer — the ray bends away from the normal and can undergo total internal reflection beyond the critical angle.

questions.stem: Which lens is used to correct short-sightedness (myopia)?
questions.explanation: In myopia the image forms in front of the retina; a diverging (concave) lens spreads the rays so the focus moves back onto the retina. Hypermetropia (long-sight) needs a converging (convex) lens. Cylindrical lenses correct astigmatism. Bifocals combine two powers for patients with presbyopia (difficulty focusing at reading distance in older age).

questions.stem: The image formed by a plane mirror is:
questions.explanation: A plane mirror always forms a virtual, erect image of the same size as the object, located at the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front. The image is laterally inverted (left becomes right) but not vertically inverted. A real image is one that can actually be caught on a screen — a plane mirror cannot produce one.

questions.stem: The focal length of a convex lens is 25 cm. Its power, in dioptres, is:
questions.explanation: Power P = 1 / f(in metres). Here f = 25 cm = 0.25 m, so P = 1/0.25 = +4 D. Convex lens → positive power; concave lens → negative. A prescription of '-2 D' means a concave lens of focal length 0.5 m.

questions.stem: Inside an optical fibre, light travels along the core by repeated:
questions.explanation: An optical fibre has a high-index core surrounded by a lower-index cladding. When light hits the core–cladding boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle, it undergoes total internal reflection and stays trapped inside the core. This lets fibres carry signals over long distances with very low loss, which is why all modern undersea and long-haul internet cables use them.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A rainbow is formed by which combination of optical phenomena acting on sunlight in water droplets?
questions.explanation: Sunlight enters a water droplet (refraction), different wavelengths bend by different amounts (dispersion), reflects once off the back of the droplet (internal reflection), and refracts again on exit. The primary rainbow shows red outside and violet inside. A fainter secondary rainbow forms when light undergoes two internal reflections — in it the colour order is reversed.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The apparent depth of a coin seen through still water is less than its real depth because of:
questions.explanation: Light from the coin bends away from the normal on leaving the water, so to the observer the coin appears shallower. The relation is Apparent depth = Real depth / n, where n is the refractive index of water (~1.33). This is the same reason a straw in a glass of water looks bent at the surface.
